summary: Directly renders 3D text with the Slug library, using fonts, layout-box controls, optional Specification DAT/CHOP rows, and normal Object COMP transform/material/render pages rather than generating SOP geometry.

key_params.name: mode
key_params.note: Use the Text parameter or a Specification DAT

key_params.name: specdat
key_params.note: Rows defining independent text blocks and parameter overrides

key_params.name: specchop
key_params.note: Numeric per-block overrides matching Specification DAT rows

key_params.name: sorted
key_params.note: Sort Specification DAT text blocks by depth for alpha blending

key_params.name: escapeseq
key_params.note: Parse escape sequences in Specification DAT text

key_params.name: wordwrap
key_params.note: Wrap text to the layout box width

key_params.name: facecam
key_params.note: Orient text to face the camera

key_params.name: layoutsize
key_params.note: Layout box size used for alignment, clipping, and wrapping

key_params.name: layoutanchor
key_params.note: Anchor point of the layout box in object space

key_params.name: drawpriority
key_params.note: Render ordering control, important for transparent glyphs

key_concepts: Geo Text COMP renders 3D text directly with the Slug text engine rather than outputting SOP geometry.
Text can come from the Text parameter, Specification DAT rows, or Specification CHOP channels.
Layout size, layout anchor, word wrap, face-camera behavior, and depth-scale controls define how text is positioned in 3D space.
Format codes, escape sequences, sorting, draw priority, and depth/lift controls help manage transparent glyph rendering.
Specification DAT/CHOP workflows require matching row/sample structure so per-string attributes such as text, transform, font size, and color line up.
common_gotchas: Geo Text COMP does not output SOP geometry; it renders glyphs directly.
The layout box substitutes for Text COMP width/height and is not visible by default.
Specification CHOP sample count must match Specification DAT data rows after the header.
Specification DAT column names must match supported parameter names such as text, tx, fontsize, or fontcolor channels.
Glyphs use blended transparent rectangles, so Draw Priority and back-to-front row order matter for correct compositing.
Depth sorting many Specification DAT text blocks can be expensive; enable it only when alpha artifacts require it.
